text:
samir (customer): Hey team — hitting 401s for some clients on our Dedicated cluster. They say Authorization header is present to the LB but missing by the time it hits the inference service. Happens only in private deployment behind Istio ingressgateway. Started after we moved to a new LB config. Can you take a look?

kevin (support): Thanks Samir. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and tell us which LB type (NLB/ALB/GCLB) + Istio version? Also any Gateway/VirtualService/EnvoyFilter changes recently?

samir (customer): Repro: 
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ..." "https://api.mycompany.internal/v1/generate" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
Response: 401 unauthorized, logs on our app pod show no Authorization header present.
LB is an internal NLB -> Istio ingressgateway -> istio-proxy (Envoy) -> backend pod. Istio 1.13. No EnvoyFilter changes that we know of.

kevin (support): Got it. Common places headers get stripped: the LB/proxy (rare for NLB), the Ingress controller, or an EnvoyFilter / Lua filter that sanitizes headers. Also check health check path — some LBs use a separate listener that can rewrite headers.

maria (eng-platform): Quick checklist: 1) curl the NLB IP directly with Host header to simulate ingressgateway behavior; 2) exec into ingressgateway pod and tcpdump on port 80/443 to confirm header arrives at pod; 3) check istio-ingressgateway logs for any header modifications; 4) if using Gateway TLS termination, ensure SNI/Host matches so request goes through correct listener.

maria (eng-platform): Example tcpdump in ingressgateway: 
kubectl -n istio-system exec -it $(kubectl -n istio-system get pod -l app=istio-ingressgateway -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- 
  bash -c "tcpdump -A -s 0 'port 443' | grep -i Authorization"

samir (customer): Ran tcpdump — I can see Authorization at LB -> ingressgateway but when I curl the cluster IP of the ingressgateway container (sidecar) the header is gone before envoy forwards to the backend.

elaine (eng-security): Two likely causes here: 1) an Envoy/istio httpConnectionManager config that explicitly removes sensitive headers; 2) a policy (RequestAuthentication/AuthorizationPolicy) that rewrites or uses JWT and prevents Authorization header forwarding. Do you have any RequestAuthentication resources that handle JWT on the gateway?

samir (customer): We do have a RequestAuthentication on the Gateway to validate tokens for some routes. But we expected the raw Authorization to be forwarded to the backend for certain internal services.

kevin (support): Important note: Istio's RequestAuthentication and AuthorizationPolicy validate tokens at the gateway level but normally do not remove the Authorization header. However, custom EnvoyFilters or Lua filters can. Also some mesh setups sanitize headers for downstream. We should check for any EnvoyFilter that patches the http_connection_manager.

maria (eng-platform): If you're ok with a quick workaround, two options: A) Have ingressgateway copy Authorization into a different header before any filters run (eg. x-forwarded-authorization) using an Envoy Lua filter; B) Configure gateway/ingress controller to preserve Authorization (nginx: proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;) where applicable.

maria (eng-platform): Example EnvoyFilter (works for Istio ingressgateway) — it adds a small Lua filter that copies Authorization to x-forwarded-authorization: 

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: forward-auth-header
  namespace: istio-system
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      istio: ingressgateway
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: GATEWAY
      listener:
        filterChain:
          filter:
            name: "envoy.filters.network.http_connection_manager"
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value:
        name: envoy.lua
        typed_config:
          "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
          inlineCode: |
            function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
              local auth = request_handle:headers():get("authorization")
              if auth ~= nil then
                request_handle:headers():add("x-forwarded-authorization", auth)
              end
            end

maria (eng-platform): After adding that, change your backend to read x-forwarded-authorization for now. This avoids fighting whatever is stripping Authorization.

samir (customer): Thanks — is that safe? Are we exposing tokens to downstream services?

elaine (eng-security): Good question. Copying the header is acceptable for internal trusted backends but you must: 1) only apply the EnvoyFilter on the ingressgateway (not all workloads), 2) limit VirtualService routing so downstream apps that should not see tokens aren't selected, 3) ensure logs and metrics do not capture full token values and redact them. Long-term we recommend token exchange (MTLS or introspection at gateway) and issuing short-lived PSK to backends.

kevin (support): Also check if any HTTP/2 upgrade or header casing transformations are happening. Some proxies normalize header names; Authorization should be case-insensitive but custom filters might remove exact-case entries.

samir (customer): Applied EnvoyFilter in istio-system -> ingressgateway. Restarted the pod, retried curl with header: backend now shows x-forwarded-authorization present and request succeeds. Looks fixed.

ops-bot: Ticket #8237 transitioned to status: investigating -> escalation -> resolved by customer.

kevin (support): Great — follow-ups: 1) if you prefer not to change backend code, we can make envoy rewrite Authorization instead of copying; 2) we should add an integration test in your CI that ensures Authorization reaches backend after gateway changes; 3) ops/security want an audit of the EnvoyFilter, can you paste the final YAML in the ticket?

maria (eng-platform): For completeness, NGINX ingress example: in the nginx config snippet add 
proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;
That forwards the original header to the upstream. For Envoy, you can also add header manipulation config to explicitly keep Authorization.

elaine (eng-security): Closing notes for the runbook: 
- Repro steps: curl to LB (check -v), tcpdump on ingressgateway, kubectl exec into ingressgateway to inspect headers, check for EnvoyFilter/RequestAuthentication/AuthorizationPolicy.
- Quick fixes: EnvoyFilter (copy or rewrite), nginx proxy_set_header, ensure LB health checks don't hit the same listener and strip headers.
- Long term: prefer gateway-level auth + token exchange to short-lived backend credentials, redact tokens in logs.

samir (customer): Thanks everyone — deploying changes to prod this afternoon. Will send the YAML into ticket #8237. Appreciate the quick help!

kevin (support): Thanks Samir, marking this thread for internal KB entry on Dedicated/Private auth header forwarding with Istio.

ops-bot: Note: add_kb_entry requested by kevin (support) — pend approval.
